STEP 1 - Scene: A light meal of a shredded lettuce/leafy salad (dressed, slightly creamy) beside two triangular slices of cheese-topped flatbread or pizza-style bread with browned spots. Photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A white square plate, roughly 26 cm across the diagonal-to-edge width. Using a side length of about 22 cm, the usable flat area is roughly 22 × 22 × 0.8 ≈ 390 cm² for the plate surface. I'll use a vessel area of about 400 cm² as the reference.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Dressed shredded lettuce/leafy greens (the pale green pile, left and top)
- Cheese-topped flatbread slice, larger piece (right, upper)
- Cheese-topped flatbread slice, smaller piece (right, lower)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Lettuce salad: ~30% of plate (about 120 cm²)
- Larger bread slice: ~12% (about 48 cm²)
- Smaller bread slice: ~11% (about 44 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 53% of plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Lettuce: 120 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 360 ml (gross envelope)
- Larger bread slice: about 8 × 6 cm footprint, 1.2 cm thick, so ~48 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 58 ml
- Smaller bread slice: ~44 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 53 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Lettuce: 360 ml × 0.15 = 54 g
- Larger bread slice: 58 ml × 0.9 = 52 g
- Smaller bread slice: 53 ml × 0.9 = 48 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Dressed lettuce: ~54 g × 35 kcal/100 g (creamy dressing adds energy) ≈ 19 kcal
- Bread with cheese: ~100 g × 260 kcal/100 g ≈ 260 kcal (cheese-topped flatbread is fairly energy-dense)

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 154 g total with roughly 280 kcal. This fits a small lunch portion: two modest flatbread slices plus a side salad. Plausible.
